taskAnchor.targetDefect: N313 authenticates the verifier and exact content subject but does not bind the signed observation to the current task dispatch, monotonic dispatch sequence, or freshness window
taskAnchor.userLastConstraint: Old artifacts or validation results cannot be presented as current work; no silent fallback; Producer and Verifier remain separate.
unknowns: Which coordinator owns the monotonic dispatch sequence
Which trusted clock source is acceptable for each execution environment
How accepted sequence state survives restart without becoming Producer-controlled
What freshness window is justified for each Mother and evidence type
forbiddenRoutes: old valid signature accepted for a later dispatch
content digest alone treated as validation freshness
Producer-supplied current time trusted without a clock route

trigger: A previously authorized and correctly signed verifier attestation is resubmitted after a later dispatch for unchanged content bytes.
expected: The signed predicate must answer the current coordinator challenge, carry the current monotonic dispatch sequence, and contain an observation time after dispatch and within the bounded freshness window.
observed: N313 returned DEPENDENCY_CLOSURE_VERIFIED for the old authorized attestation because subject, predicate type, signature, authority, and context still matched.
rootCause: N313 proves who signed what, but not when or for which dispatch the observation was produced.
minimumVerification: old signed attestation on a new verificationRequestId returns HOLD_VERIFIER_CHALLENGE_MISMATCH
signed predicate with an old dispatch sequence returns HOLD_VERIFIER_DISPATCH_SEQUENCE_ROLLBACK
observation time before dispatch returns HOLD_STALE_VERIFIER_ATTESTATION
observation older than the bounded maximum age returns HOLD_STALE_VERIFIER_ATTESTATION
observation time beyond allowed future skew returns HOLD_VERIFIER_TIME_INVALID
fresh signed observation for the current challenge and sequence passes
a rolled-back task anchor is rejected against persisted trusted sequence state

stateSemantics.HOLD_VERIFIER_CHALLENGE_MISMATCH: Signed evidence answers a different verification request.
stateSemantics.HOLD_VERIFIER_DISPATCH_SEQUENCE_ROLLBACK: Dispatch or attestation sequence is not newer than trusted state or does not match the current anchor.
stateSemantics.HOLD_STALE_VERIFIER_ATTESTATION: Observation predates dispatch or exceeds the bounded freshness window.
stateSemantics.HOLD_VERIFIER_TIME_INVALID: Observation time is malformed or exceeds allowed future clock skew.
stateSemantics.DEPENDENCY_CLOSURE_VERIFIED: Authorized evidence is bound to the current challenge, monotonic sequence, exact subject, and valid freshness window.

teacherCandidate.name: The Update Framework rollback and freeze protections
teacherCandidate.boundedDomain: recognizing stale but validly signed metadata through monotonic trusted version state and expiry
teacherCandidate.noveltyAnswer: N313 proves signature authority but treats every still-valid signature as current. TUF explicitly separates authenticity from freshness: clients persist trusted versions, reject rollback, and reject expired metadata against a fixed update-start time.

screening.sourceProvenance: Official TUF specification, security documentation, and theupdateframework GitHub organization.
screening.maintenance: Specification v1.0.37 released 2026-10-08 with repository activity observed through 2026-10-16; python-tuf v7.0.1 released 2026-09-01 with repository activity observed on 2026-11-18.
screening.runnableEvidence: Versioned specification, Python reference implementation, repository simulator, generated/repository test data, API tests, examples, and release tooling are present.
screening.licenseAndRights: Specification uses Community Specification License 1.0; python-tuf is dual Apache-2.0/MIT. No external assets are required for this protocol trial.
screening.directRelevance: Directly models replay of old signed evidence as rollback/freeze rather than a signature failure.
screening.noveltyVsCurrentBestView: KAOPU's no-stale gate requires post-dispatch validation, but N313 has no monotonic trusted state, challenge, or signed expiry semantics.
screening.integrationRisk: The prototype has no external dependency. Full python-tuf would require Python 3.11+, securesystemslib and urllib3 and would be excessive; real adoption instead needs trusted time, persistent state, challenge generation, crash recovery, and bounded per-Mother windows.
screening.failureRisks: TUF cannot guarantee an update under withholding; it detects possible freeze. Trusted-clock failure, lost state, malicious version fast-forward, and copied semantics without persistence can recreate the bypass.

deduplication.TASK_FRESHNESS_AND_NO_STALE_DELIVERY_GAT: Already states that validation must run after dispatch. N314 transfers that rule into signed verifier evidence and supplies executable states.
deduplication.TERRAIN_NO_STALE_DELIVERY_001: Covers stale production artifacts and screenshots; N314 covers cryptographically valid but stale verifier attestations.
deduplication.N313: Authenticates origin and authorization but not dispatch freshness.

boundaries: The verification request IDs and times are synthetic fixtures, not production challenge or clock services.
Freshness does not prove observation truth, visual correctness, device correctness, or user acceptance.
A trusted clock and persisted sequence state are required; Producer-controlled values do not close the gate.
Freshness windows must be selected per bounded evidence type rather than globally imposed.
The Candidate borrows rollback/freeze principles, not the full TUF updater architecture.
No production Mother, main, R2 OS, adapter registry, or public KaoPuGram service changes.
